examples.en: The bottle's opening was narrow, so I used a funnel.

examples.ko: 기름을 부을 때는 깔때기가 있으면 편해요.
examples.en: It's easier when you have a funnel for pouring oil.

examples.ko: 깔때기 없이 부었더니 바닥에 다 흘렀어요.
examples.en: I poured it without a funnel and spilled it all over the floor.

examples.ko: 주방 서랍에서 작은 깔때기 좀 꺼내 주세요.
examples.en: Please take a small funnel out of the kitchen drawer.

examples.ko: 종이를 깔때기 모양으로 말아서 소금을 넣었어요.
examples.en: I rolled the paper into a funnel shape and poured in the salt.

examples.ko: 이 깔때기는 구멍이 작아서 물이 천천히 내려가요.
examples.en: This funnel has a small hole, so the water goes down slowly.

explain: 주방뿐 아니라 과학 실험이나 자동차에 기름을 넣을 때도 자주 나와요. 위는 넓고 아래는 좁은 모양을 말할 때 '깔때기 모양'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It appears not only in the kitchen but also in science experiments and when putting oil into a car. People also say '깔때기 모양' for anything wide at the top and narrow at the bottom.

examples.en: The rice stuck to the pot, so it's hard to wash.
Gum got stuck to my shoe.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마한테 딱 들러붙어서 안 떨어져요.
examples.en: The child clings to the mom and won't let go.
It's uncomfortable when wet clothes cling to your body.

examples.ko: 파리가 음식에 들러붙지 않게 덮어 두세요.
examples.en: Cover the food so flies don't land and stay on it.
The egg is going to stick to the frying pan.

explain: 들러붙다는 '붙다'보다 끈적하게 꽉 붙어서 잘 안 떨어지는 느낌이 강해요. 사람에게 쓰면 계속 따라다니며 귀찮게 한다는 부정적인 뜻이 돼요. 활용은 규칙이라 '들러붙어요', '들러붙었어요'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 들러붙다 feels stickier and harder to pull off than plain '붙다'. Used about people it is negative, meaning to cling and keep bothering someone. It conjugates regularly: '들러붙어요', '들러붙었어요'.

examples.en: Cold wind comes in through the gap in the door.
My finger got caught in the door gap and it hurt.
The gap around the door is wide, so bugs come in.
Light leaked out through the crack in the door.
I sealed the door gap with tape, and it's less cold now.
I heard laughter through the crack in the door.

explain: 문과 문틀 사이처럼 좁게 벌어진 곳이에요. '문틈으로 엿보다', '문틈에 끼이다', '문틈으로 바람이 들어오다'처럼 짝지어 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the narrow gap between a door and its frame. It pairs naturally with phrases like '문틈으로 엿보다' (peek through the crack), '문틈에 끼이다' (get caught in the gap) and '문틈으로 바람이 들어오다' (wind comes through).

examples.en: I took the Christmas decorations out of the box.
I made this ornament myself.
The ornaments hanging on the tree are sparkling.
I hung a small picture as a wall decoration.
Dust has piled up on the decorations.

examples.ko: 장식물 하나 때문에 방 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The room's mood changed because of a single ornament.

explain: 꾸미기 위해 놓거나 다는 물건을 두루 가리켜요. '장식품'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 둘 다 집이나 행사 분위기를 꾸밀 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It broadly refers to things placed or hung for decoration. '장식품' is used in a similar way, and both come up often when decorating a home or an event.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 문고리를 잡을 때 정전기가 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: In winter, static often builds up when I grab a door handle.

examples.ko: 스웨터를 벗었더니 머리카락이 정전기 때문에 곤두서요.
examples.en: I took off my sweater, and my hair stands up from the static.
I sprayed anti-static spray on my clothes.
My fingertip stung, so I thought it was static.
Static happens easily on dry days.

examples.ko: 차에서 내릴 때마다 정전기에 깜짝 놀라요.
examples.en: Every time I get out of the car, the static makes me jump.

explain: '정전기가 일어나다', '정전기가 생기다'처럼 써요. 건조한 겨울에 많이 느끼고, 그때의 따끔한 느낌은 '따끔하다'나 '찌릿하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: You say 정전기가 일어나다 or 정전기가 생기다 for static building up. People notice it most in dry winter air, and the sting is described with 따끔하다 or 찌릿하다.

examples.en: The police officer blew a whistle and stopped the car.

examples.ko: 체육 선생님이 호루라기를 불자 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: When the gym teacher blew the whistle, everyone gathered.
I was startled by the sound of a whistle.

examples.ko: 등산할 때 위급하면 호루라기를 불어서 알려요.
examples.en: When hiking, if there's an emergency, blow a whistle to signal.

examples.ko: 목에 호루라기를 걸고 있는 사람이 심판이에요.
examples.en: The person with a whistle around his neck is the referee.

examples.ko: 호루라기가 고장 났는지 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: It doesn't make a sound, so the whistle may be broken.

explain: 도구로 부는 '호루라기'는 '불다'와 함께 써요. 입술로 내는 소리는 '휘파람'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 심판, 경찰, 선생님이 신호를 줄 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The device '호루라기' goes with the verb '불다' (blow). A whistle made with your lips is '휘파람', which is different. It often appears with referees, police, and teachers giving signals.
